author: maatheusgois-dd
body:
### Summary
This PR addresses Swift Concurrency compilation errors and unused return value warnings that were preventing successful builds with Swift 5.9+ strict concurrency checking enabled.

### Changes Made

#### 1. Fixed Sendable Closure Error in WKWebViewNetworkMonitor.swift
**Problem**: `[String: Any]` is not Sendable, causing compilation failure when captured in `@Sendable` closures.

**Solution**: 
- Created `WebViewRequestInfo` struct that conforms to `Sendable`
- Implemented proper type-safe data storage with Sendable types:
  - `String` for request ID, URL, method, body
  - `Date` for timing information
  - `[String: String]` for headers
- Maintained API compatibility through `toDictionary()` and `from` initializer
- Updated `WebViewRequestCache` to use the new Sendable struct internally

**Files Modified**: `DebugSwift/Sources/Features/Network/Helpers/WKWebViewNetworkMonitor.swift`

#### 2. Fixed Unused Return Value Warnings in Network.ViewModel.swift
**Problem**: Return values from `addHttpRequest` calls were unused, generating compiler warnings.

**Solution**: 
- Added `_ =` prefix to explicitly discard return values
- This occurs in the `handleClearAction` method when re-adding requests after clearing operations

**Files Modified**: `DebugSwift/Sources/Features/Network/Main/Network.ViewModel.swift`

### Technical Details

#### Swift Concurrency Fix
The core issue was that `[String: Any]` cannot be captured in `@Sendable` closures because `Any` can contain non-Sendable types. The solution provides:

1. **Type Safety**: All stored data is now explicitly typed as Sendable types
2. **Data Conversion**: Proper handling of various body data types (String, Dictionary, etc.) to Sendable equivalents
3. **API Compatibility**: Existing code continues to work without changes
4. **Performance**: Clean data structure without unnecessary overhead

#### Compiler Warning Fix
The unused return value warnings were addressed by explicitly discarding the boolean return values from `addHttpRequest` calls, which indicate whether the request was successfully added to the datasource.

### Testing
- ✅ Project builds successfully with Swift Concurrency enabled
- ✅ All linter warnings resolved
- ✅ No functional changes to existing behavior
- ✅ Backward compatibility maintained

### Impact
- **Build Success**: Resolves compilation failures with modern Swift versions
- **Code Quality**: Eliminates compiler warnings
- **Future-Proof**: Ensures compatibility with Swift 6 when strict concurrency becomes mandatory
- **Maintainability**: Cleaner, more type-safe code structure

### Breaking Changes
None. All changes are backward compatible.

---

**Labels**: `bugfix`, `swift-concurrency`, `compiler-warnings`, `network-monitoring`

author: deboer-tim
body:
Fixes two problems:
- PlaybackContest had its own configurationLoaded property, which never gets set: all non-admin clients would wait for 2s regardless of config being loaded. It now uses the property from the parent contest object.
- Synchronized accountContests means that the playback contest is blocked from adding objects while we're waiting for account to load... which blindly waits for 2s as per above. i.e. we weren't letting the main contest load config at all. It now spreads the objects to each account directly (multiple listeners) instead of from the main listener.

Hi all - I was looking through the codebase to help create the first ASF release (#1336) and thought we might benefit from a little clean-up. Please have a look and let me know if I went too far  with anything - happy to roll things back!

 NOTE: This is a follow-up to  the closed issue #1371 

## Changes

- [x] Moved top-level images to new `assets` folder. Do we need to keep these?
- [x] Moved top-level md files to either `docs` or `writeups`. Maybe these should be fully integrated with the docs?
- [x] Deleted `setup.py`, removing the legacy Python packaging script and related logic
- [x] Remove unused configuration files (`.style.yapf`, `.flake8`, ...)
- [x] Update manifest (remove non-existent requirements files)
- [x] Update min required python to `3.8.1`. This allows contributors to use `uv sync` without allowing prereleases (as per the last meetup, I would like bump the min required python to `3.9` next)
- [x] Update `uv` configuration. Since `pip` now has support, I moved dev dependencies to `dependency-groups` (PEP 735)
- [x] Fix broken tests ~(maybe out of scope for this PR)~

## How I tested this

No changes to codebase

## Notes

N/A

## Checklist

- [x] PR has an informative and human-readable title (this will be pulled into the release notes)
- [x] Changes are limited to a single goal (no scope creep)
- [x] Code passed the pre-commit check & code is left cleaner/nicer than when first encountered.
- [x] Any _change_ in functionality is tested
- [x] New functions are documented (with a description, list of inputs, and expected output)

author: copilot
body:
This PR upgrades the backend LLM from Claude 3 Haiku to Claude Sonnet 3.5 v2 to improve Fijian language processing capabilities.

## Problem

The current implementation uses Claude 3 Haiku (`anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0`), which has been identified as weak at native Fijian language processing. Claude Sonnet 3.5 v2 provides significantly stronger performance for multilingual tasks, especially for low-resource languages like Fijian.

## Changes Made

Updated the model identifier in all three Lambda functions that use Claude:

- **Chat Lambda** (`backend/lambdas/chat/src/handler.ts`): Updated `CLAUDE_MODEL_ID` constant
- **RAG Lambda** (`backend/lambdas/rag/src/handler.ts`): Updated `CLAUDE_MODEL_ID` constant  
- **Vocabulary Management Lambda** (`backend/lambdas/vocabulary-management/index.ts`): Updated `modelId` in Bedrock request
- **Documentation** (`README.md`): Updated references from Claude 3 Haiku to Claude Sonnet 3.5 v2

## Model Change

```diff
- const CLAUDE_MODEL_ID = 'anthropic.claude-3-haiku-20240307-v1:0';
+ const CLAUDE_MODEL_ID = 'anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0';
```

## Impact

- **Performance**: Significantly improved Fijian language understanding and generation
- **Cost**: Moderate increase in per-token cost, offset by better quality requiring fewer retries
- **Compatibility**: No breaking changes - same API contracts maintained
- **Deployment**: Ready for immediate deployment with no infrastructure changes required

All builds and tests pass successfully. The change is minimal and surgical, affecting only the model identifier while preserving all existing functionality.

Fixes #126.

author: copilot
body:
This PR completely remakes the maze application to implement the requested enhanced features while maintaining the core maze generation functionality.

## 🎯 Problem Statement
The original maze needed to be enhanced with:
- Start and end points at the furthest locations in the maze
- Checkbox to hide walls of unvisited cells
- Checkbox for automatic movement with intelligent pathfinding and backtracking
- HTML-based interface with modern UI controls

## 🚀 Solution Overview

### **1. Furthest Points Algorithm**
Implemented a BFS-based distance calculation system that:
- Tests every cell as a potential starting point
- Calculates distances to all reachable cells using breadth-first search
- Identifies the pair of cells with maximum separation distance
- Sets these as the true start (light blue) and end (light coral) positions

### **2. Hide Unvisited Walls Feature**
Added a checkbox that dynamically controls wall rendering:
- Tracks player's visited cells using a Set data structure
- Conditionally renders walls only around explored areas
- Creates a unique "fog of war" effect showing exploration progress

### **3. Intelligent Automatic Movement**
Implemented sophisticated pathfinding logic:
- **Single Path**: Automatically moves when only one unvisited neighbor exists
- **Dead End**: Backtracks through visited cells until finding a choice point
- **Multiple Paths**: Stops and waits for manual user input
- **Visual Feedback**: Shows visited path in gray color

### **4. Enhanced User Interface**
Redesigned the layout with:
- Container-based responsive design
- Styled checkboxes with hover effects
- Improved button styling and spacing
- Clean visual hierarchy

## 🔧 Technical Implementation

**Key Functions Added:**
```javascript
// Find maximum distance between any two cells
function findFurthestPoints()

// BFS distance calculation
function bfsDistances(startCell)

// Checkbox event handlers
function toggleUnvisitedWalls()
function toggleAutoMovement()

// Intelligent movement logic
function performAutoMovement()
function backtrackToChoice()
```

**Enhanced Rendering:**
- Modified `drawCell()` to show start/end positions and visited state
- Updated `drawWalls()` to conditionally hide walls based on exploration
- Added visited cell tracking throughout movement functions

## 📸 Screenshots

**Before - Original Maze:**
![Original](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9d27e29-06db-4535-85ab-896f1a205e9e)

**After - Enhanced Maze with Furthest Points:**
![Enhanced](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d185cf7d-ede1-4765-9a3c-6421b3ce7f38)

**Hide Unvisited Walls Feature:**
![Hide Walls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bec2553c-cd27-4bf4-9778-19402110bf78)

**Automatic Movement in Action:**
![Auto Movement](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c1cdcf2-0244-4540-9d17-04d83e3d9dc2)

## ✅ Testing
- ✅ Furthest points algorithm correctly identifies maximum distance pairs
- ✅ Hide walls checkbox toggles wall visibility properly
- ✅ Automatic movement handles all scenarios (single path, dead ends, multiple choices)
- ✅ Manual keyboard controls continue to work when auto-movement is disabled
- ✅ Both features work independently and in combination
- ✅ Player wins detection works with new end positions

## 🎮 How to Use
1. **Generate Maze**: Creates new maze with furthest start/end points
2. **Hide Unvisited Walls**: Check to see only explored areas
3. **Automatic Movement**: Check to enable intelligent pathfinding
4. **Manual Control**: Use arrow keys when auto-movement is off
5. **Victory**: Reach the coral-colored end position to win!

The enhanced maze provides a much more engaging and intelligent exploration experience while maintaining the original game's core mechanics.

author: nathanchica
body:
This pull request introduces a sliding window expiration mechanism for refresh tokens, improving session management and security. The changes update both backend logic and documentation to support refresh tokens that extend their expiration on use, up to an absolute maximum lifetime. Environment configuration, database schema, and authentication flow documentation are all updated to reflect these enhancements.

**Authentication & Token Management**

* Added sliding window expiration for refresh tokens: tokens now extend their expiration by 7 days on each use, up to a maximum of 30 days, and are deleted if inactive or past the absolute maximum. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-765ff18853bfda6dcabada7b2b0191f45a8a8bc158fa32f38c897f8258020c37L103-R118) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-765ff18853bfda6dcabada7b2b0191f45a8a8bc158fa32f38c897f8258020c37R135-R174)
* Updated environment variables and config validation to support new sliding window and absolute max settings (`REFRESH_TOKEN_SLIDING_DAYS`, `REFRESH_TOKEN_ABSOLUTE_MAX_DAYS`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0ab7147cd8ad1eddcd936d4014fc9778eb565a51aed784bbdd32ffcba52cf22bR21-R24) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-034fceb2c27c3df1390f6c3de6d072e80cab2e1e88538ec901e2e3aed5266b8fL19-R24) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ce3676ececf6328207cb53b4acdcdfe34fcc4ebb7a986cce7394ab9bfb54d4f2R11-R12)

**Database Schema**

* Modified the `RefreshToken` model to include `absoluteExpiresAt`, `isActive`, and an index for `absoluteExpiresAt` to support sliding window logic and session tracking.

**Documentation**

* Significantly revised the authentication flow in `README.md` to explain the new access/refresh token system, sliding window expiration, mutation examples, and frontend integration details. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-31a92f1c67f6af74712cadf88311a65463655d4ff829634f77dfa7434ef29dc2L272-R337) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-31a92f1c67f6af74712cadf88311a65463655d4ff829634f77dfa7434ef29dc2R349-R389) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-31a92f1c67f6af74712cadf88311a65463655d4ff829634f77dfa7434ef29dc2R66-R73)

**Testing & Mocks**

* Updated test setup and mocks to support new refresh token structure and environment variables, including a utility for creating mock refresh tokens with sliding and absolute expiration. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-987a05bc3712688045a4be38836897ee8b15242444a8464baf644d239184fb4dR2) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-987a05bc3712688045a4be38836897ee8b15242444a8464baf644d239184fb4dR24-R42) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ce3676ececf6328207cb53b4acdcdfe34fcc4ebb7a986cce7394ab9bfb54d4f2R11-R12)

author: technicalpickles
body:
## Overview

This PR implements a **streamlined and simplified** automated release workflow that builds cross-platform binaries with native ARM64 runners, eliminating cross-compilation complexity. The implementation includes comprehensive Docker-based development environment and standardized Rust toolchain management.

## ✨ Key Features

### 🎯 **Native ARM64 Build Strategy**
- **Native ARM64 runners**: Uses `ubuntu-24.04-arm` for ARM64 Linux builds
- **Eliminates cross-compilation**: Each architecture builds natively for better reliability
- **Universal macOS binaries**: Still creates universal binaries using `lipo` from native builds
- **Simplified workflow**: Reduced complexity compared to cross-compilation approaches

### 🔄 **Automated Release Process**
- **Trigger**: Monitors `Cargo.toml` version changes on main branch
- **Multi-platform builds**: Linux (x64/ARM64), macOS (Universal)
- **Automatic releases**: Creates GitHub releases with binaries, checksums, and release notes
- **Zero manual intervention**: Just bump the version and push to main

### 🐳 **Docker Development Environment**
- **Complete development setup**: Ubuntu 22.04 based with mise tool management
- **Cross-platform development**: Consistent environment across different host systems
- **Helper scripts**: `scripts/dev-docker.sh` for easy container management

### 🛠 **Standardized Rust Toolchain**
- **Single source of truth**: `rust-toolchain.toml` defines Rust 1.89.0 across all environments
- **Consistent targets**: Pre-installed targets for all supported platforms
- **LLD linker optimization**: Faster builds with LLD linker support

## 📦 Release Artifacts

| Binary | Platform | Architecture | Build Method |
|--------|----------|-------------|-------------|
| `envsense-v{version}-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` | Linux | x64 | Native |
| `envsense-v{version}-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` | Linux | ARM64 | Native ARM64 runner |
| `envsense-v{version}-universal-apple-darwin` | macOS | Universal | lipo from native builds ⭐ |

Plus SHA256 checksums for all binaries.

## 🛠 Key Scripts

#### **`scripts/build-target.sh`**
- Universal binary creation using `lipo`
- Native builds for each target
- Verification of universal binary architecture

#### **`scripts/install_lld.sh`**
- Cross-platform LLD installation (macOS via Homebrew, Ubuntu via apt)
- Environment setup for GitHub Actions

#### **`scripts/dev-docker.sh`**
- Development container management
- Multiple shell support (bash/fish)
- Test and build commands

## 🐳 Docker Development Workflow

```bash
# Build development environment
./scripts/dev-docker.sh build

# Start interactive development session
./scripts/dev-docker.sh run

# Inside container: all tools pre-configured
cargo build --release
cargo test --all
```

## 🎯 Key Improvements

### ✅ **Eliminated Cross-Compilation Complexity**
- Native builds on appropriate runners for reliability
- No more complex cross-compilation setup

### ✅ **Standardized Rust Toolchain** 
- Single `rust-toolchain.toml` ensures consistency
- Rust 1.89.0 across all environments

### ✅ **Simplified Docker Environment**
- Clean development-focused environment with mise
- Easy onboarding with one command

### ✅ **Native ARM64 Support**
- Native ARM64 runners instead of cross-compilation
- Better compatibility and performance

## 🧪 Validation Results

- ✅ **Native builds**: All targets build successfully on appropriate runners
- ✅ **Universal binaries**: macOS universal binaries verified with `lipo -info`
- ✅ **Script testing**: Comprehensive validation across all platforms
- ✅ **Workflow validation**: Passes `actionlint` without warnings
- ✅ **Docker environment**: Development container builds and runs correctly

## 🚀 Usage

### For Development
```bash
# Docker development (recommended)
./scripts/dev-docker.sh build
./scripts/dev-docker.sh run

# Native development
mise install  # Installs Rust 1.89.0
cargo build --release
```

### For Releases
1. Update version in `Cargo.toml`
2. Commit and push to main
3. GitHub Actions automatically creates release

## 🎉 Production Ready

- ✅ **Simplified architecture**: Native builds eliminate issues
- ✅ **Standardized toolchain**: Consistent Rust 1.89.0
- ✅ **Docker development**: Easy onboarding
- ✅ **Universal macOS support**: Single binary for all Macs
- ✅ **LLD optimization**: Faster builds

The next version bump will trigger the streamlined release process! 🚀

author: copilot
body:
Successfully converted the entire BeamShare P2P file transfer application from Node.js to Java Spring Boot while maintaining 100% feature parity and frontend compatibility.

## Key Changes

**Backend Migration:**
- Converted Express.js server to Spring Boot with embedded Tomcat
- Migrated WebSocket implementation from `ws` package to Spring WebSocket
- Translated all server logic from JavaScript to Java:
  - `server.js` → `BeamShareWebSocketHandler.java` (780+ lines of WebSocket handling)
  - `peer.js` → `Peer.java` (peer management and device info)
  - `helper.js` → `DeviceInfoHelper.java` (utility functions)

**Technology Stack:**
- **Framework:** Spring Boot 3.2.0
- **WebSocket:** Spring WebSocket with `/ws` endpoint
- **Build System:** Maven with `pom.xml`
- **Java Version:** 17+

**Frontend Compatibility:**
- Zero changes required to existing HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend
- Same WebSocket message protocol maintained
- All features preserved: device discovery, P2P file transfer, room sharing, QR codes
- Material Design UI fully functional

## Technical Implementation

The Java implementation maintains the exact same WebSocket message format and API, ensuring seamless compatibility:

```java
// WebSocket handler maintains same message types
switch (type) {
    case "join-ip-room":
        joinIpRoom(peer);
        break;
    case "peerjs-id-update":
        handlePeerJSIdUpdate(peer, message);
        break;
    // ... all original message types supported
}
```

**Project Structure:**
```
src/main/java/com/beamshare/
├── BeamShareApplication.java      # Spring Boot main class
├── config/WebSocketConfig.java    # WebSocket configuration
├── controller/BeamShareWebSocketHandler.java  # Main WebSocket logic
├── model/Peer.java               # Peer model with device info
└── util/DeviceInfoHelper.java    # Device detection utilities
```

## Benefits of Java Migration

- **Enterprise Ready:** Better integration with Java-based enterprise systems
- **Performance:** JVM optimizations and mature garbage collection
- **Tooling:** Rich IDE support and debugging capabilities
- **Ecosystem:** Access to extensive Java libraries and Spring ecosystem
- **Deployment:** Easy deployment to Java application servers
- **Scalability:** Built-in Spring Boot clustering and scaling features

## Testing & Validation

- ✅ All tests pass: `mvn test` (2/2 successful)
- ✅ Application builds successfully: `mvn clean package`
- ✅ Server starts correctly on port 3000
- ✅ WebSocket connections established properly
- ✅ Full UI functionality verified
- ✅ Device discovery and file transfer working

The application can now be run with:
```bash
mvn spring-boot:run
# or
npm run java:start
```

<screenshot>
![Java BeamShare Application](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e92e4714-f3d2-4e65-9c66-348dda8c64cb)

*BeamShare successfully running on Java Spring Boot with Material Design UI and Vietnamese localization*
</screenshot>

Fixes #2.

author: copilot
body:
Este PR implementa completamente el módulo de Oportunidades para el CRM Salud, transformando una funcionalidad básica en un sistema completo de gestión del pipeline de ventas.

## 🎯 Funcionalidades Implementadas

### Gestión Completa de Oportunidades
- **Lista de oportunidades** con filtros avanzados por estado y cliente
- **Creación de oportunidades** con formulario dinámico que carga clientes y usuarios
- **Edición completa** con datos precargados y validación
- **Eliminación AJAX** con confirmación de usuario
- **Vista detallada** mostrando información completa e historial de actividades

### Pipeline de Ventas Visual
- **Tablero Kanban** con 7 etapas del ciclo de ventas:
  - Prospecto → Contactado → Calificado → Propuesta → Negociación → Ganado/Perdido
- **Estadísticas en tiempo real** por cada etapa del pipeline
- **Transiciones de estado** intuitivas desde el tablero
- **Indicadores visuales** de fechas vencidas y probabilidades

### Integración con Módulos Existentes
- **Clientes**: Asociación automática con información de tipo y contacto
- **Usuarios**: Asignación de responsables del equipo de ventas
- **Comunicaciones**: Historial de interacciones relacionadas
- **Calendario**: Actividades programadas vinculadas a oportunidades

## 🔧 Cambios Técnicos

### Modelos Mejorados
```php
// Nuevos métodos en Oportunidad.php
getOportunidadConRelaciones($id)      // Datos con joins a clientes/usuarios
getOportunidadesConRelaciones()       // Lista con relaciones
getEstadisticasPipeline()            // Stats para dashboard Kanban
getComunicacionesOportunidad($id)    // Historial de comunicaciones
getActividadesOportunidad($id)       // Actividades relacionadas
```

### Controlador Completo
- `OportunidadesController::store()` - Creación con validación completa
- `OportunidadesController::update()` - Actualización con manejo de estados
- `OportunidadesController::delete()` - Eliminación AJAX segura
- `OportunidadesController::kanban()` - Vista de pipeline visual

### Vistas Responsivas
- **index.php**: Lista con filtros, estadísticas y tabla responsive
- **kanban.php**: Tablero visual con drag-and-drop style
- **create.php**: Formulario dinámico con selección de clientes/usuarios
- **edit.php**: Formulario precargado con datos existentes
- **view.php**: Vista detallada con historial de actividades

## 📊 Pipeline Visual

![Pipeline Kanban](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f77a7cb-831c-4124-b8a2-823c04329439)

El tablero Kanban proporciona una vista visual del pipeline de ventas con:
- Tarjetas de oportunidades organizadas por etapa
- Estadísticas resumidas por columna (cantidad, valor total, probabilidad promedio)
- Indicadores de fechas vencidas y estados críticos
- Acciones rápidas para ver/editar cada oportunidad

## 🗄️ Base de Datos

### Migración Requerida
```sql
-- Agregar campo faltante para prioridades
ALTER TABLE `oportunidades` 
ADD COLUMN `prioridad` enum('baja','media','alta') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'media' AFTER `probabilidad`;
```

La tabla `oportunidades` existente ya contiene todos los campos necesarios para el ciclo de ventas completo.

## ✨ Características Destacadas

- **Diseño responsive** que funciona en móviles y tablets
- **Integración nativa** con la arquitectura MVC existente
- **Seguridad robusta** con validación de entrada y protección XSS
- **Performance optimizada** con consultas JOIN eficientes
- **UX intuitiva** siguiendo patrones de Bootstrap 5

## 🔗 Compatibilidad

- ✅ **Base de datos**: Compatible con MySQL existente
- ✅ **Arquitectura**: Utiliza BaseModel y BaseController
- ✅ **Frontend**: Bootstrap 5 y Bootstrap Icons existentes
- ✅ **Navegación**: Integrado en el menú principal
- ✅ **Permisos**: Utiliza sistema de autenticación actual

Este módulo transforma la gestión de oportunidades de un placeholder a una herramienta completa de CRM que permite al equipo de ventas visualizar, gestionar y hacer seguimiento efectivo de todo el pipeline comercial.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

*This pull request was created as a result of the following prompt from Copilot chat.*
> Desarrolla el módulo de Oportunidades con las siguientes funcionalidades:
> - Listar oportunidades comerciales abiertas, ganadas y perdidas.
> - Crear, editar y eliminar oportunidades.
> - Asociar oportunidades a clientes, productos y usuarios responsables.
> - Seguimiento de etapas del ciclo de ventas (lead, análisis, propuesta, cierre).
> - Registro de actividades y notas dentro de cada oportunidad.
> - Visualización de pipeline (tablero Kanban).
> Asegura compatibilidad con la estructura actual y base de datos MySQL. Mantén la integración adecuada con los módulos de clientes y usuarios.

author: rakshabesafe
body:
This commit introduces a full suite of testing tools to improve the project's reliability and developer workflow, addressing the need to test individual components and Celery tasks both in isolation and in an integrated environment.

The following key additions and changes have been made:

1.  **Updated CPU Task Unit Tests (`tests/unit/test_tasks_cpu.py`):**
    -   Refactored existing tests to align with the current Celery task dispatching logic (using `send_task` and `apply_async` instead of `chord`).
    -   Updated function signatures to match the latest implementation of the `assemble_video` task.

2.  **Rewritten GPU Task Unit Tests (`tests/unit/test_tasks_gpu.py`):**
    -   The outdated test file was completely replaced with modern, robust unit tests.
    -   New tests were added for the `AudioSynthesisService` to test its core logic in isolation.
    -   New tests for the `synthesize_audio` Celery task were added, correctly mocking the task context and dependencies to verify flow control and error handling.

3.  **New Integration Test (`tests/integration/test_celery_task_invocation.py`):**
    -   Added a new integration test that runs against a live Docker environment.
    -   It specifically tests the `assemble_video` task's interaction with the MinIO service by uploading dummy data, invoking the task, and verifying the final video output.

4.  **New Standalone GPU Task Runner (`test_gpu_task_runner.py`):**
    -   Created a new script to allow developers to manually trigger a `synthesize_audio` task on the GPU worker from outside the Docker environment.
    -   The script connects to the Celery broker, dispatches the task, and polls for the result, providing a direct way to test the GPU pipeline.

5.  **Updated `README.md`:**
    -   Added a new "Testing" section to the main `README.md`.
    -   This section provides clear, step-by-step instructions for:
        -   Installing test dependencies.
        -   Running the full unit test suite.
        -   Running the integration tests.
        -   Using the standalone GPU task runner, including prerequisite setup.

6.  **Updated Test Dependencies:**
    -   Added `Pillow` to `requirements-test.txt` to support the creation of dummy image data for tests.

body:
This PR implements a complete coffee machine management backend system as specified in the requirements (咖啡管理后台系统改进方案), transforming the basic system into a production-ready IoT device management platform.

## 🚀 Major Features Implemented

### RESTful API for Device Communication
Added a comprehensive client API suite (`/api/v1/client/*`) with 16 endpoints covering the complete device lifecycle:

- **Authentication**: Secure device registration and JWT token-based authentication
- **Status Reporting**: Real-time device metrics (temperature, water level, pressure, cups made)
- **Command Control**: Bidirectional command dispatch and result reporting
- **Configuration Management**: Remote device configuration with templates
- **Maintenance**: Log upload, update checking, and health monitoring

```python
# Example: Device status reporting
POST /api/v1/client/status
{
  "status": "online",
  "temperature": 85.5,
  "water_level": 80.0,
  "pressure": 9.0,
  "cups_made_today": 25,
  "material_status": {"coffee": 80, "milk": 60}
}
```

### WebSocket Real-time Communication
Implemented full-duplex WebSocket communication supporting:

- **Device Channels**: Real-time status updates and instant command delivery
- **Admin Channels**: Live monitoring dashboard with event broadcasting
- **Connection Management**: Session tracking, heartbeat mechanism, and automatic cleanup
- **Event Broadcasting**: Real-time notifications for device online/offline, errors, and command results

### Enhanced Security Framework
Built enterprise-grade security features:

- **Rate Limiting**: Configurable request throttling (1000 requests/hour normal, 100 requests/hour strict)
- **Security Headers**: CSP, HSTS, XSS protection, and frame options
- **Audit Logging**: Comprehensive security event tracking with severity levels
- **Secure API Keys**: Cryptographically secure 32-byte key generation

### Advanced Monitoring Dashboard
Created sophisticated monitoring APIs (`/api/v1/monitoring/*`) providing:

- **Real-time Overview**: Live device statistics with online rates and performance metrics
- **Device Management**: Advanced filtering, search, and grouping capabilities
- **Performance Analytics**: Historical trend analysis and device performance tracking
- **Batch Operations**: Multi-device command dispatch and configuration management

## 🛠 Technical Implementation

### Database Enhancements
Extended the data model with new entities:

- **Enhanced Device Model**: Added API authentication fields, IP tracking, and configuration storage
- **MachineStatus Model**: Detailed device metrics with timestamps
- **MachineLog Model**: Structured logging with context and severity levels
- **ClientCommand Model**: Priority-based command queue with timeout support

### WebSocket Architecture
```python
# Real-time device authentication
socketio.emit('device_auth', {'api_key': 'device_api_key'})

# Live status broadcasting to admins
broadcast_to_admins('device_status_update', {
    'device_no': 'CM001',
    'status': device_metrics,
    'timestamp': '2024-01-01T10:00:00Z'

body:
Docker imageで使用しているCUDAのバージョンをv12系からv13系に更新しました。

## 変更内容

`Docker/reranker-server/Dockerfile`の2箇所のFROM文を更新:

**変更前:**
```dockerfile
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu24.04 AS builder
FROM nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu24.04
```

**変更後:**
```dockerfile
FROM nvidia/cuda:13.0.0-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu24.04 AS builder
FROM nvidia/cuda:13.0.0-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu24.04
```

## 技術詳細

- **CUDAバージョン**: 12.8.1 → 13.0.0
- **ベース環境**: ubuntu24.04 + cuDNN runtime（変更前と同一構成を維持）
- **変更範囲**: ベースイメージのCUDAバージョンのみ、アプリケーション機能は無変更
- **対象サービス**: reranker-server

## 検証結果

- ✅ nvidia/cuda:13.0.0-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu24.04 イメージの取得確認済み
- ✅ Docker起動時に "CUDA Version 13.0.0" の表示確認済み
- ✅ 最小限の変更（2行のみ）で要件達成

この変更により、より新しいCUDA v13系の機能とパフォーマンス向上を利用できるようになります。

Fixes #13.

Noticed when forking off of master there are 2 test failures that show up that don't show up here. This will fix those tests for everyone. Fixes two failing tests in AlertReportModal.test.tsx:
- "renders 5 checkmarks for a valid alert" (expected 5, received 3)
- "does not show screenshot width when csv is selected" (couldn't find "test chart" text)

 Root cause analysis revealed three interconnected issues:

1. **Icon accessibility bug**: BaseIcon genAriaLabel function produced incorrect aria-labels due to regex split creating empty strings ("CheckCircleOutlined" → [""," Check","Circle","Outlined"] → "-check" instead of "check-circle")

  2. **Incomplete test data**: validAlert mock was missing required validation fields for AlertReportModal's 5 validation sections (database, sql, validator_config_json, working_timeout, chart objects)

  3. **Data structure mismatch**: Test mock used MetaObject format but AlertReportModal's data processing pipeline expected fallback domain object properties (slice_name, database_name) when getChartData/getDatabaseData return null

  - Added complete validation data for all 5 AlertReportModal sections

body:
## Problem
The Creative Commons (CC) icons in the Content License section of the README were too large and inconsistent with the surrounding text font size. The icons used `max-width: 1em; max-height: 1em;` styling which made them appear oversized and poorly aligned with the text baseline.

## Solution
Updated the CC icon styling to use more appropriate dimensions and alignment:

**Before:**
```html
style="max-width: 1em;max-height:1em;margin-left: .2em;"
```

**After:**
```html
style="height: 0.85em; vertical-align: text-bottom; margin-left: .2em;"
```

## Changes Made
1. **Precise size control**: Changed from `max-height: 1em` to `height: 0.85em` for better size consistency
2. **Improved alignment**: Added `vertical-align: text-bottom` to align icons properly with the text baseline
3. **Better proportions**: Reduced size from 1em to 0.85em, making the icons more proportional to the text

## Visual Comparison
![CC Icons Comparison](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebdf699c-661e-4faf-ad90-e5fe2e72c696)

The change is minimal and surgical - only one line modified in the README.md file - ensuring the CC license icons now display at an appropriate size that's consistent with the font and properly aligned with the text baseline.

body:
This PR adds automated AI-powered issue triage capabilities to the java-debug repository by incorporating the triage agent workflow and LLM documentation from the vscode-gradle repository.

## Changes Made

### Added Files
- **`.github/workflows/triage-agent.yml`** - GitHub Actions workflow that automatically labels and comments on new issues using AI
- **`.github/llms.md`** - Documentation containing guidelines for LLM-based issue labeling and Java extension context

### Key Features
- **Automatic Issue Triage**: The workflow triggers on new issue creation and can also be run manually via workflow dispatch
- **AI-Powered Labeling**: Uses Azure Function integration to analyze issue content and apply appropriate labels
- **Java Extension Context**: Includes comprehensive documentation about the Java extension ecosystem to guide proper issue categorization

### Configuration Updates
- Updated the `repoId` from `microsoft/vscode-gradle` to `microsoft/java-debug` to ensure the triage agent correctly identifies this repository
- Maintained all existing error handling, timeout management, and HTTP status validation from the original workflow

### Dependencies
The workflow requires the following repository secrets to be configured:
- `GITHUB_TOKEN` - For GitHub API access (automatically provided)
- `TRIAGE_FUNCTION_LINK` - Azure Function endpoint URL
- Repository variable `TRIAGE_AGENT_TIMEOUT` - Timeout configuration for the triage agent

This enhancement will help maintainers by automatically categorizing new issues, reducing manual triage effort, and ensuring consistent labeling across the repository.

body:
This PR addresses critical character encoding issues (乱码) that were causing garbled Chinese text in the deploy preview, while maintaining the single-file architecture approach.

## Problem Fixed

The previous single-file implementation suffered from UTF-8 encoding corruption during the embedding process, causing Chinese characters to display as garbled text in the deployed version. The file had also grown to over 5000 lines, making it difficult to maintain.

## Solution

Created a clean, properly encoded single-file version with enhanced UTF-8 support:

- **Fixed UTF-8 Encoding**: Resolved character encoding issues that caused 乱码 (garbled text)
- **Enhanced Browser Compatibility**: Added UTF-8 BOM (Byte Order Mark) for improved encoding detection
- **Chinese Font Support**: Integrated Chinese-friendly font stack with PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei (微软雅黑), and fallbacks
- **Clean Architecture**: Reduced from 5000+ to 505 lines while preserving all functionality
- **Proper Embedding**: All configurations and styles embedded without encoding corruption

## Key Features

The consolidated HTML file includes:
- **Configuration**: All AppConfig settings embedded directly with proper UTF-8 handling
- **Styling**: Complete CSS with Chinese font support and encoding safeguards
- **Functionality**: Working React components for customer interface and admin login
- **Integrations**: WhatsApp ordering, Supabase connectivity, FontAwesome icons
- **Admin Features**: Password visibility toggle, management interface

## Technical Details

- UTF-8 BOM for universal browser encoding detection
- Multiple charset declarations (`<meta charset="UTF-8">` and HTTP-equiv)
- Chinese-optimized font stack: `'PingFang SC', 'Hiragino Sans GB', 'Microsoft YaHei', '微软雅黑', 'SimSun', '宋体'`
- Clean JavaScript embedding without character corruption
- Responsive design with mobile-first approach
- Error handling for library loading failures
- Supabase database integration with member system support

The solution maintains deployment simplicity as a single HTML file while ensuring Chinese characters display correctly across all browsers, servers, and deployment environments through multiple encoding safeguards.

author: copilot
body:
This PR addresses a security vulnerability identified by the ZIZMOR security scanner that flagged credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts.

## Problem

The ZIZMOR security check was failing with warnings like:
```
warning[artipacked]: credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts
  --> /github/workspace/.github/workflows/super-linter.yaml:35:7
   |
35 |       - name: "Get the common linters configuration"
   |  _______-
36 | |       uses: actions/checkout@v4
...  |
40 | |         sparse-checkout: |
41 | |           config/linters
   | |________________________- does not set persist-credentials: false
```

## Solution

Added `persist-credentials: false` to all 26 instances of `actions/checkout@v4` and `@v5` across 19 workflow files. This security parameter prevents credentials from being persisted through GitHub Actions artifacts, which is a security best practice.

## Changes Made

For actions without existing `with:` blocks:
```yaml
# Before:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4

# After:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    persist-credentials: false
```

For actions with existing `with:` blocks:
```yaml
# Before:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0

# After:
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
    persist-credentials: false
```

## Files Updated

- `.github/workflows/super-linter.yaml` (2 instances)
- `.github/workflows/create-github-release.yml`
- `.github/workflows/maven-central-snapshot-deploy-reusable.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/auto-labeler.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/re-npm-publish.yml`
- `.github/workflows/pr-conventional-commits.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/scout-repo-scan.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/link-checker.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/github-release.yaml` (2 instances)
- `.github/workflows/automatic-pr-labeler.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml`
- `.github/workflows/re-maven-snapshot-deploy.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/release-drafter.yml`
- `.github/workflows/pr-assigner.yml`
- `.github/workflows/go-check-license.yaml`
- `.github/workflows/python-publish.yml`
- `.github/workflows/maven-publish.yml`
- `.github/workflows/broadcast-files.yml` (6 instances)
- `.github/workflows/tag-creator.yml`

## Verification

- All 26 instances now include `persist-credentials: false`
- YAML syntax validation passed for all modified files
- No functional changes to workflow behavior - only security enhancement

This change ensures compliance with security scanning tools and follows GitHub Actions security best practices.

Fixes #322.

author: eljonny
body:
Between 0.2.9 and 0.3.0, there were changes in dependencies that caused
 the types to become incompatible between Uint8Array and
 FileSystemWriteChunkType where the base compatible type is ArrayBuffer
 but Uint8Array is based on ArrayBufferLike, which can be an
 ArrayBuffer but also can be a number of other incompatible types, and
 is thus incompatible with FileSystemWriteChunkType.

I introduced a compatibility layer (Adapter Pattern-like) to copy the
 buffer into an ArrayBuffer if it is not an ArrayBuffer, otherwise just
 use the buffer if it already is.

Closes #203.

author: copilot
body:
The hydration errors on admin organization pages were caused by invalid HTML structure where `BreadcrumbSeparator` components (which render as `<li>` elements) were wrapped inside `BreadcrumbItem` components (also `<li>` elements), creating nested `<li>` elements.

This invalid nesting caused server-rendered HTML to differ from client-rendered HTML, triggering React hydration mismatches with console warnings like:

```
Warning: Expected server HTML to contain a matching <li> in <ol>.
```

## Changes Made

Fixed the breadcrumb structure in 4 files by removing the `BreadcrumbItem` wrapper from `BreadcrumbSeparator`:

**Before (Invalid):**
```tsx
<BreadcrumbList>
  <BreadcrumbItem>Item</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
  </BreadcrumbItem>
</BreadcrumbList>
```

**After (Valid):**
```tsx
<BreadcrumbList>
  <BreadcrumbItem>Item</BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbSeparator />
</BreadcrumbList>
```

## Files Modified

- `src/pages/Admin/organizations/AdminOrganizationList.tsx` - 2 instances fixed
- `src/pages/Facility/settings/organizations/FacilityOrganizationList.tsx` - 2 instances fixed  
- `src/pages/Organization/components/OrganizationLayout.tsx` - 1 instance fixed
- `src/pages/Facility/settings/locations/LocationView.tsx` - 1 instance fixed

The fix maintains the same visual appearance and functionality while creating valid HTML structure that prevents hydration mismatches.

Fixes #13552.

author: mnemonikr
body:
## Why is this change being proposed?

I was fuzzing the .sla parser in the decompiler and resolved a number of issues uncovered. I've included all of the fixes in this PR, but if preferred I can split this into multiple PRs. I tried to keep each commit self-contained to the issue I was resolving for easier reviewing.

### Heap buffer overflows

These all triggered Address Sanitizer bug reports prior to being fixed:

1. There is a buffer overflow in `PackedDecode::advancePosition` due to the signed skip parameter, which is read from the `.sla` file. If negative, can result in a read out of bounds. This was changed to unsigned.
2. Identifiers read from the file and used as indexes should be validated to not exceed the container size. These included the symbol list, symbol scope table, address spaces, and constructors.

### Null pointer dereferences

1. If `endIngest` is called without any additional data, calls to `decode` will result in null deref when `getByte` tries to deref `endPos.current` which isn't set to point to the input stream (since there isn't one allocated). This can be triggered by an `.sla` file with just the header. I changed `endIngest` here to throw an exception in this case.
2. Symbol list and symbol scope tables updated to ensure their entries are non-null before deleting in destructor.
3. Pattern expression decoder returned null if invalid, but none of the callers checked for it. Changed this to an exception.

### Memory leaks

These were issues identified by Leak Sanitizer and largely followed the pattern

```cpp
TypeToDecode * localVar = new TypeToDecode();
localVar->decode(...);
owner->var = localVar;
```

If an issue occurred in `decode`, the `localVar` type would never be destroyed. These were largely mitigated with the use of `std::unique_ptr` locally to ensure the value would be destroyed on exception. The unique pointer is released prior to returning to prevent unwanted destruction on success.

The other common memory leak was overwriting the same value if decoding the same id multiple times. These scenarios were turned into exceptions. However, if there is a usecase for these, can update to change to free the previous value and allow overwriting instead.

## Additional changes

The following files were not technically a part of the fuzz run but exhibited the same decoding pattern that resulted in the memory leaks elsewhere. I've included patches for these that should resolve the same style of memory leaks on decoding failure.

* architecture.cc
* funcdata.cc
* modelrules.cc

Improve worker count calculation for `"auto"` concurrency.

<!--

-->

refs https://github.com/eslint/eslint/discussions/20040#discussioncomment-14222589

<!--
    Please ensure your pull request is ready:

    - Read the pull request guide (https://eslint.org/docs/latest/contribute/pull-requests)
    - Include tests for this change
    - Update documentation for this change (if appropriate)
-->

<!--
    The following is required for all pull requests:
-->

#### What changes did you make? (Give an overview)

This pull request makes some improvements to the thread count calculation that is done when the concurrency is `"auto"`.

1. Ignored files are no longer considered in the thread count calculation. Determining if a file is ignored can be done very efficiently now because config arrays are pre-loaded for all files when the files are enumerated.
2. When using the cache with the default "metadata" strategy, cached files with unchanged results are no longer considered in the thread count calculation. This means that only files which need to be read, parsed and processed by the linter will be counted. If all cached results are valid, multithreading will not be used. 
3. Increased the `AUTO_FILES_PER_WORKER` constant from 35 to 50. This constant value affects the thread count calculation when only a few files are linted. The most visible effect is that multithreading will be no longer turned on when linting less than 51 files (this is an empiric value and possibly still too low on some machines). I realized that some of the projects I used in my early tests were biased by ignored files. After repeating the tests with ignored files not counted, the larger value seems more appropriate.
 
#### Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?

The additional time to count files that need processing (excluding ignored and cached files) is printed in a debug line, for example:

```shell
  eslint:eslint 351 file(s) to process counted in 18 ms +19ms
```

In practice, the effective overhead seems to be even lower, possibly because of cross-thread caching by the OS, which results in subsequent access to file metadata being faster.

#### Benchmarks

I tested the implementation on a fork of the OpenUI5 repo which contains 12,500 lintable files and uses the `--cache` option: https://github.com/mauriciolauffer/openui5/tree/eslint-v9.

These are the results when the cache file is outdated:

```shell
> time DEBUG=eslint:eslint eslint ./src --quiet --cache --concurrency=auto
  eslint:eslint Using config loader LegacyConfigLoader +0ms
  eslint:eslint Using file patterns: ./src +0ms
  eslint:eslint 12500 file(s) found in 4009 ms +4s
  eslint:eslint 151 file(s) to process counted in 3 ms +3ms
  eslint:eslint Linting using 4 worker thread(s). +0ms
DEBUG=eslint:eslint eslint ./src --quiet --cache --concurrency=auto  139.43s user 8.25s system 526% cpu 28.039 total
```

It takes just 3 milliseconds to determine that the maximum number of threads (i.e. 4 for an 8 core CPU) should be used.

Now, here are the results when the cache file is present and all cached results are valid:

```shell
> time DEBUG=eslint:eslint eslint ./src --quiet --cache --concurrency=auto

author: copilot
body:
The Docker build pipeline for desktop containers was failing with an invalid tag format error:

```
ERROR: failed to build: invalid tag "ghcr.io/owasp/wrongsecrets/:master": invalid reference format
```

The root cause was incorrect matrix variable references in the `desktop-container-publish.yml` workflow. The matrix is defined with a `container` key containing an array of objects:

```yaml
strategy:
  matrix:
    container:
      - name: "webdesktop"
        dockerfile: "Dockerfile_webdesktop"
        image_name: "wrongsecrets-desktop"
      - name: "webdesktop-k8s"
        dockerfile: "Dockerfile_webdesktopk8s"
        image_name: "wrongsecrets-desktop-k8s"
```

However, the workflow was using `matrix.image_name` instead of `matrix.container.image_name`, causing the variable to be undefined and resulting in malformed Docker tags like `ghcr.io/owasp/wrongsecrets/:master`.

**Changes made:**
- Fixed `matrix.image_name` → `matrix.container.image_name`
- Fixed `matrix.dockerfile` → `matrix.container.dockerfile`
- Fixed `matrix.name` → `matrix.container.name`

**Before:** `ghcr.io/OWASP/wrongsecrets/` + undefined + `:master` → `ghcr.io/owasp/wrongsecrets/:master` ❌

**After:** `ghcr.io/OWASP/wrongsecrets/wrongsecrets-desktop:master` ✅

The fix ensures proper Docker image naming for both the `wrongsecrets-desktop` and `wrongsecrets-desktop-k8s` container variants.

Fixes #2228.

author: bitsforpeace
body:
## What does this PR do?

This PR implements widget-specific network tracking for multichain widgets in the Sky Protocol app. The feature addresses a UX issue where users lose their preferred network context when navigating between widgets.

### Problem Solved
Previously, when users navigated from a multichain widget (e.g., Savings on Base) to a mainnet-only widget (e.g., Upgrade) and then back to the original widget, they would remain on mainnet instead of returning to their preferred network (Base).

### Implementation Details

**Key Changes:**
- Extended `NetworkSwitchContext` to track network preferences per widget during the session
- Modified `WidgetNavigation` component to save/restore network states when switching between widgets
- Updated `ChainModal` to track manual network changes for the current widget

**Tracking Behavior:**
- **Trade & Savings widgets**: Each maintains its own network preference independently
  - When leaving: Current network is saved for that specific widget
  - When returning: Widget's previously saved network is restored
- **Balances widget**: Explicitly excluded from tracking - always stays on the current network
- **Mainnet-only widgets** (Upgrade, Rewards, Stake, Expert, Seal): Continue to force mainnet as before

**Session Scope:**
- Network preferences are stored in React state (session-only)
- No browser storage is used
- All preferences are cleared on page refresh

### Files Modified
- `/apps/webapp/src/modules/ui/context/NetworkSwitchContext.tsx` - Added widget network state management
- `/apps/webapp/src/modules/app/components/WidgetNavigation.tsx` - Implemented save/restore logic
- `/apps/webapp/src/modules/ui/components/ChainModal.tsx` - Added tracking for manual network changes

## Testing Steps

1. **Test independent widget tracking:**
   - Navigate to Trade widget and switch to Optimism
   - Navigate to Savings widget and switch to Base
   - Navigate to Stake widget (forced to mainnet)
   - Navigate back to Trade → **Should restore Optimism** (not Base from Savings)
   - Navigate to Savings → **Should restore Base**

2. **Test Balances widget exclusion:**
   - Navigate to Trade and set to Arbitrum
   - Navigate to Balances (stays on Arbitrum)
   - Manually switch to Base while in Balances
   - Navigate to Upgrade (forced to mainnet)
   - Navigate back to Balances → **Should stay on mainnet** (no restoration)
   - Navigate to Trade → **Should restore Arbitrum**

3. **Test mainnet-only to multichain transitions:**
   - Navigate to Savings and set to Base
   - Navigate to Upgrade (forced to mainnet)
   - Navigate back to Savings → **Should restore Base**

4. **Test multichain to multichain navigation:**
   - Navigate to Trade (no saved state, on mainnet)
   - Switch to Arbitrum
   - Navigate to Savings (no saved state) → **Should stay on Arbitrum**
   - Navigate back to Trade → **Should stay on Arbitrum** (same as saved)

5. **Test manual network switching updates:**
   - Navigate to Trade and switch to Optimism
   - Manually switch to Base using the network switcher
   - Navigate to Rewards (forced to mainnet)
   - Navigate back to Trade → **Should restore Base** (the manually selected network)

6. **Test session persistence:**
   - Set different networks for Trade (Optimism) and Savings (Base)
   - Navigate between various widgets to confirm states persist
   - Refresh the page
   - Navigate to Trade → **Should not restore** (cleared on refresh)
   - Navigate to Savings → **Should not restore** (cleared on refresh)

7. **Test edge cases:**
   - Rapidly switch between widgets to ensure no race conditions
   - Test with network switch failures (reject in wallet) - state should remain consistent
   - Navigate directly via URL changes to ensure tracking still works

### Expected Behavior Summary
- Trade and Savings each remember their own last-used network
- Balances never saves or restores, always uses current network  
- Network preferences are widget-specific, not shared between widgets
- Manual network changes update the saved state for the current widget
- All tracking is session-only and clears on page refresh

This pull request refactors how required directories are created for the MelonService application. Instead of creating directories in the Dockerfiles, the logic is now moved into the application code to ensure proper initialization at startup. This makes the directory management more robust and compatible with Docker volumes.

**Directory management improvements:**

**Dockerfile changes:**

* Updated both `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.dev` to stop creating `Logs`, `Temp`, and `Output` directories, since these will now be managed as Docker volumes and initialized by the application itself. Instead, a placeholder `/tmp/init` directory is created to maintain Docker build consistency. ### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>moonrepo/moon (@​moonrepo/cli)</summary>

### [`v1.39.4`](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1394)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/compare/@moonrepo/cli@1.39.3...@moonrepo/cli@1.39.4)

##### 🐞 Fixes

-   Fixed an issue with `moon setup` failing when proto is not available.
-   Fixed task input inferrence to not include the `$HOME`, `$USER`, and `$PWD` environment variables.
-   Fixed some arg/shell quoting issues.

### [`v1.39.3`](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1393)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/compare/@moonrepo/cli@1.39.2...@moonrepo/cli@1.39.3)

##### 🐞 Fixes

-   Fixed a regression where an unknown/unconfigured `layer` would trigger a violation error.

### [`v1.39.2`](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1392)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/compare/@moonrepo/cli@1.39.1...@moonrepo/cli@1.39.2)

##### 🐞 Fixes

-   Fixed a glob input parsing issue when the pattern contained a `?` and wasn't in URI format.
-   Fixed JSON schemas not including property aliases (project `type` for `layer`, etc).

##### ⚙️ Internal

-   Updated dependencies.

### [`v1.39.1`](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1391)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/compare/@moonrepo/cli@1.39.0...@moonrepo/cli@1.39.1)

##### 🐞 Fixes

-   Fixed a path error for `@moonrepo/cli` package.

### [`v1.39.0`](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1390)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/compare/@moonrepo/cli@1.38.6...@moonrepo/cli@1.39.0)

##### 🚀 Updates

-   The automatic proto install has moved into a new `SetupProto` action, which is now part of the
    action graph, and does not run on every command. It's also a bit smarter and will only install
    when a toolchain requires it.
-   Added support for new task input formats based on the RFC:
[https://github.com/moonrepo/moon/issues/1985](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/moon/issues/1985)1985
    -   Added URI support for files (`file://`) and globs (`glob://`).
    -   Added object support for files and globs.
-   Updated task input files:
    -   Added a `optional` param, which allows the file to be optional (missing) during hashing.
        Defaults to true.
    -   Added a `content` param, which will match against the file's contents to determine affected
        state.
-   Updated task input globs:
    -   Added a `cache` param, which controls whether the glob results should be cached or not.
-   Updated the `@moonrepo/cli` npm package to no longer rely on postinstall scripts.
-   Improved argument quoting for commands and scripts.
-   Renamed project `type` to `layer`, as it better reflects what it does, a layer of access within
    the project `stack`. For backwards compatibility, the `type` name will still be supported until
    v2. The following changes have been made:
    -   `type` -> `layer` in `moon.yml`
    -   `--type` -> `--layer` in `moon query projects`
    -   `projectType` -> `projectLayer` for MQL
    -   `$projectType` -> `$projectLayer` for task tokens
    -   `enforceProjectTypeRelationships` -> `enforceLayerRelationships` in `.moon/workspace.yml`

##### 🐞 Fixes

-   Fixed `moon query touched-files --defaultBranch` requiring a "true" or "false" explicit value.

##### ⚙️ Internal

-   Added telemetry for toolchain usage.
-   Added unstable support for bubbling up logs from WASM plugins.
-   Updated Rust to v1.88.0.
-   Updated proto to [v0.51.4](https://redirect.github.com/moonrepo/proto/releases/tag/v0.51.0) (from 0.50.1).
-   Updated dependencies.

</details>

body:
In the schema of `com.circleci.v2`, it's declaring its configuration parameter of `no_output_timeout` as Pkl's [Duration](https://pkl-lang.org/package-docs/pkl/current/base/Duration.html) type. However, given type was not configured in `converters` configuration, therefore Pkl's YAML renderer couldn't render the value.

According to CircleCI documentation, `no_output_timeout` is defined as follows. I've added some some conversion rule by making `min` as only special case.
> Elapsed time the command can run without output. The string is a decimal with unit suffix, such as "20m", "1.25h", "5s".

refs:
* https://circleci.com/docs/reference/configuration-reference/

author: discostur
body:
- fixes https://github.com/grafana/helm-charts/issues/3867

**Description:**
This PR fixes a YAML parsing error that occurs when rendering the Grafana Helm chart with sidecar searchNamespace values.

**Problem:**
When using searchNamespace: ["ALL"] or similar values in sidecar configurations, the template rendering produced invalid YAML with double quotes like value: ""ALL"", causing the error:

```bash
Error: YAML parse error on grafana/templates/deployment.yaml: error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: line 99: did not find expected key
```

**Solution:**
Updated the template syntax in _pod.tpl for all sidecar NAMESPACE environment variables from:

```bash
value: "{{ tpl (. | join ",") $root }}"
```
to
```bash
value: {{ tpl (. | join ",") $root | quote }}

body:
# Pull Request Description

## Summary
This PR improves CI safety and fixes YAML parsing issues. Fixes #31 

## Changes
- **Add sanity checks** to verify that the compiled binary’s `--version` output matches:
  - `Cargo.toml` version  
  - Debian upstream version in `debian/changelog`  
  - Git tag version (on tagged builds)  
- **Build & check release binary before packaging**, then also verify the binary inside the generated `.deb`.  
- **Fix YAML syntax errors** by quoting step names containing colons (`:`).  

## Why
- Prevents mismatches where a stale or misconfigured build could ship with the wrong version string.  
- Ensures that CI fails fast if versioning is inconsistent.  
- Keeps the workflow YAML valid across all runners.

body:
## Issue

- resolve: https://github.com/route06/liam-internal/issues/5495

## Why is this change needed?

This refactoring addresses structural inconsistencies in the `frontend/internal-packages/agent` package by consolidating duplicate directory purposes, flattening unnecessary nesting, and creating uniform import paths across the codebase.

## Summary of Changes

### Directory Structure Reorganization
- **Dissolved `chat/workflow/` directory**: Redistributed files to eliminate deep nesting
  - `shared/workflowAnnotation.ts` → `src/annotations.ts`
  - `shared/workflowConstants.ts` → `src/constants.ts`  
  - `shared/getConfigurable.ts` → `src/utils/getConfigurable.ts`
  - `utils/*` → `src/utils/*`
  - `types.ts` → merged into `src/types.ts`

- **Consolidated `shared/` into `utils/`**: Eliminated duplicate directory purposes
  - Moved `errorHandling.ts`, `jsonSchema.ts`, `traceEnhancer.ts`, `workflowSetup.ts`

- **Dissolved `langchain/utils/`**: Redistributed specialized utilities
  - `schema.ts` → `src/utils/validationSchema.ts`
  - `types.ts` → merged into `src/types.ts`

### Import Path Updates
- Updated 50+ files with new import paths throughout agents, scripts, and tests
- Standardized on shorter, more intuitive import paths (e.g., `../utils/` vs `../chat/workflow/utils/`)

### Code Quality Improvements
- **Fixed WorkflowTerminationError constructor**: Unified to single string argument format across all usage
- **Removed unused dependencies**: Eliminated `@valibot/to-json-schema` and unused exports
- **Preserved git history**: Used `git mv` commands to maintain file history through the restructuring

## Files Changed
- 59 files total (223 insertions, 498 deletions)
- All TypeScript compilation, linting, and dependency checks pass

## Critical Areas for Review

⚠️ **High Priority**: This refactoring touches nearly every file in the agent package. Please focus on:

1. **End-to-end functionality testing** - Verify that actual agent workflows (PM, DB, QA, Lead) still function correctly, as structural changes like this can introduce runtime issues not caught by static analysis

2. **JsonSchema functionality** - The `@valibot/to-json-schema` dependency was replaced with a stub implementation. Verify this doesn't break any functionality that relies on proper JSON schema generation


3. **Error handling verification** - All `WorkflowTerminationError` constructor calls were changed from 2 arguments to 1. Spot check that error handling still works correctly in critical paths

4. **Import dependency validation** - With extensive import path changes, verify no circular dependencies were introduced and all imports resolve correctly at runtime

5. **Type system integrity** - Multiple type files were merged into `src/types.ts`. Ensure no type conflicts or missing exports were introduced

---

**Issue**
Resolves #10971


**Approach**
The callback from `ropt` into the run model was only used to check if the user aborted the optimization. This was superseded by a different mechanism and this callback was in fact never called anymore. Optimization is now simply terminated without informing `ropt`. This has no negative consequences on the optimizer that `ropt` is running, it is simply terminated, hence this approach is sufficient and the callback is not necessary anymore.

author: marrouchi
body:
# Motivation
This PR introduces a safer, cross-tab–aware reconnect() for our Socket.IO client.
It uses the Web Locks API to serialize reconnection attempts across tabs, adds timeouts and error handling, and ensures listener cleanup so the lock is never held indefinitely. It also switches state checks to socket.connected for correctness.

## Problem

When multiple tabs try to reconnect at the same time, we can:
- spin up parallel WS handshakes and duplicate server-side session work,
- deadlock if connect never fires (no timeout / no reject),
- leak listeners, keeping the lock until reload,
- rely on socket.active, which is not a reliable indicator of connection state.

## Solution
- Wrap the reconnect flow in navigator.locks.request('ws_connection', { mode: 'exclusive' }, …) to serialize attempts across tabs.
- Use a promise with timeout (default: 10s) and listen to connect, connect_error, and error to resolve/reject deterministically.
- Always cleanup (remove listeners + clear timeout) in a finally block to guarantee lock release.
- Prefer socket.connected to short-circuit when already connected and to decide if we should force a fresh handshake.
- Graceful fallback: if Web Locks isn’t available, run the reconnect logic without a lock (behavior matches current, but with safer timeout/error handling).

## Other updates
- Prevent from subscribing multiple times to broadcast channel when we have multiple renders
- Prevent "get started" from being sent multiple times

This PR updates [more-itertools](https://pypi.org/project/more-itertools) from **4.2.0** to **10.8.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 10.8.0
   ```
   ------

* New functions:
    * :func:`derangements` was added (thanks to debruijn)
    * :func:`argmin` and :func:`argmax` were added (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`running_median` was added (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`extract` was added (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`interleave_randomly` was added (thanks to ktbarrett)

* Changes to existing functions:
    * The type hints and docstring for :func:`batched` were improved (thanks to qobilidop and inventshah)
    * The memory usage of :func:`islice_extended` was reduced (thanks to ben42code)
    * The performance of :func:`sample` and :func:`consecutive_groups`, :func:`dft`, :func:`idft`, :func:`map_if`, :func:`count_cycle`, and :func:`tail` were improved (thanks to rhettinger) 
    * The performance of :func:`before_and_after`, :func:`mark_ends`, and :func:`interleave_longest` were improved (thanks to pochmann3) 
    * :func:`nth_prime` now accepts an ``approximate`` keyword. When set to ``True``, a faster but less accurate method is used to return a result. (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`last` now works when its input has ``__reversed__`` set to ``None`` (thanks to inventshah)
    * The :func:`unzip` function was simplified (thanks to pochmann3)
    * The :func:`reshape` function now accepts ``shape`` values that represent multidimensional matrices (thanks to rhettinger)

* Other changes:
    * An issue with dark themes and documentation display was fixed (thanks to pochmann3, moreati, and pradyunsg)
    * Variable names in several functions were improved (thanks to rhettinger)
    * The docstrings for :func:`dft`, :func:`idft`, :func:`minmax`, :func:`sample`, and :func:`multinomial` were improved (thanks to rhettinger)
    * Packaging and package index metadata were improved (thanks to cdce8p)
    * Several aspects of the documentation were improved (thanks to rhettinger, saadmanrafat)
    * The Makefile now refers to `python` instead of `python3` (thanks to ktbarrett)
    * Test coverage was improved (thanks to rhettinger)
    * Python 3.14 is now tested by GitHub Actions
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 10.7.0
   ```
   ------

* New functions:
    * :func:`multinomial` was added (thanks to rhettinger)

* Changes to existing functions:
    * :func:`ichunked`, :func:`iterate`, :func:`one`, :func:`only`, :func:`powerset_of_sets`, and :func:`strictly_n` were optimized (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`exactly_n` now uses less memory (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`dft` and :func:`idft` were optimized for Python versions below 3.12 (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`is_prime` no longer shares state with the users random number generator (thanks to rhettinger)

* Other changes:
    * Some docstring issues were fixed (thanks to lpulley and ricbit)
    * The type hints for :func:`groupby_transform` were improved (thanks to rhettinger)
    * The ``furo`` theme is now used for docs (thanks to AA-turner)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 10.6.0
   ```
   ------

* New functions:
    * :func:`is_prime` and :func:`nth_prime` were added (thanks to JamesParrott and rhettinger)
    * :func:`loops` was added (thanks to rhettinger)

* Changes to existing functions:
    * :func:`factor` was optimized to handle larger inputs and use less memory (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`spy` was optimized to enable nested calls (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`polynomial_from_roots` was made non-recursive and able to handle larger numbers of roots (thanks to pochmann3 and rhettinger)
    * :func:`is_sorted` now only relies on less than comparisons (thanks to rhettinger)
    * The docstring for :func:`outer_product` was improved (thanks to rhettinger)
    * The type annotations for :func:`sample` were improved (thanks to rhettinger)

* Other changes:
    * Python 3.13 is officially supported. Python 3.8 is no longer officially supported. (thanks to hugovk, JamesParrott, and stankudrow)
    * `mypy` checks were fixed (thanks to JamesParrott)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 10.5.0
   ```
   ------

* Bug fixes
    * A missing symbol in ``more.pyi`` was fixed (thanks to eberts-google and nathanielmanistaatgoogle)

* Other changes
    * :func:`all_equal` was optimized (thanks to pochmann3 and rhettinger)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 10.4.0
   ```
   ------

* Changes to existing functions
    * :func:`circular_shifts` now accepts a ``steps`` parameter (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`distinct_permutations` now accepts iterables with non-comparable items (thanks to hgustafsson, JamesParrott, and pochmann3)
    * :class:`run_length`, :func:`totient`, :func:`sliding_window`, and :func:`triplewise` were optimized (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :class:`ilen` was optimized (thanks to pochmann3 and rhettinger)
    * :func:`sample` was improved, and now accepts ``counts`` and ``strict`` parameters (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`set_partitions` now accepts ``min_size`` and ``max_size`` parameters (thanks to Pandede)
    * :func:`seekable`'s ``relative_seek`` method remembers previous calls (thanks to dkrikun)
    * :func:`sort_together` now accepts a ``strict`` parameter (thanks to rhettinger and Pandede)

* Other changes
    * The docs for :func:`is_sorted` and :func:`strictly_n` were improved (thanks to pochmann3 and fakuivan)
    * The typing information for :func:`windowed_complete`, :func:`zip_broadcast`, and :func:`zip_equal` were improved (thanks to m472, eyalho, akisatoon1, jbosboom, and Pandede)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 10.3.0
   ```
   ------

* New functions
    * :func:`powerset_of_sets`, :func:`dft`, and :func:`idft` (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`join_mappings` (thanks to NeilGirdhar and rhettinger)
    * :func:`doublestarmap` (thanks to Skeen, monk-time, DamianB-BitFlipper, and ergoithz)
    * :func:`unique` (thanks to rhettinger)

* Changes to existing functions
    * :func:`collapse`, :func:`chunked_even`, :func:`ichunked`, :func:`padded`, and :func:`windowed` were optimized and improved (thanks to james-wasson)
    * :func:`totient` was optimized (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`roundrobin` was updated and improved (thanks to rhettinger)
    * :func:`all_equal` now accepts a *key* parameter.
    * The docs for :func:`value_chain` were improved (thanks to bjrtx)
    * The type annotations for :class:`countable` were improved (thanks to aidanholm)

* Other changes
    * Unit tests were improved (thanks to haukex)
    * Some documentation issues were fixed (thanks to bjrtx and DimitriPapadopoulos)

* New functions

    * :func:`takewhile_inclusive` was refactored (thanks to eltoder)

    * :func:`nth_permutation`, :func:`nth_combination_with_replacement`, :func:`combination_index`, and :func:`combination_with_replacement_index` were optimized (thanks to rhettinger)

body: Strengthen Odos V2 swap adapters to prevent stuck funds and mitigate reentrancy. Previously, a flaw in swap adapters could lead to user funds getting stuck if the input amount differed from the actual swap amount. This PR fixes this by introducing a pre-swap balance sufficiency check, refining the post-swap leftover collateral validation to ensure the exact input is consumed, and adding a `nonReentrant` guard to the `swapDebt` function in `OdosDebtSwapAdapterV2`. ---

author: tomaszwojcikowski
body:
### Problem
When users with Stream Management (XEP-0198) enabled go offline, MongooseIM fails to send presence unavailable notifications to their subscribers. This affects both clean disconnections (explicit unavailable presence) and network failures, breaking XMPP presence subscriptions and violating RFC 6121 specifications.

**Symptoms:**
- Subscribers don't receive `<presence type="unavailable"/>` when stream management users go offline
- Presence states become inconsistent across the system
- Users appear online indefinitely to their contacts despite being disconnected

### Root Cause
Hook priority conflict between `mod_stream_management` and `mod_presence`:
- `mod_stream_management` registered its `user_terminate` hook with priority `50`
- `mod_presence` registered its `user_terminate` hook with priority `90` 
- Lower priority numbers execute first, so stream management was stopping processing before presence could send unavailable notifications

### Solution

#### 1. Hook Priority Fix
**File:** mod_stream_management.erl
- Changed `user_terminate` hook priority from `50` to `100`
- This ensures `mod_presence` (priority 90) executes before stream management cleanup
- Allows proper presence unavailable broadcasting before session termination

#### 2. Enhanced Presence Broadcasting Logic
**File:** mod_presence.erl
- Added `presence_broadcast_filtered/3` function to handle different termination scenarios
- **Clean shutdown with resume**: Broadcasts to others but skips self-routing
- **Session replacement**: Avoids sending to the replacing session PID while notifying other resources
- **Other terminations**: Uses standard presence broadcasting

#### 3. Session Manager Enhancement  
**File:** ejabberd_sm.erl
- Added `get_user_present_resources_and_pids/1` function
- Enables precise resource and PID tracking for multi-resource users
- Supports filtered presence broadcasting during session replacement

#### 4. Comprehensive Test Coverage
**File:** sm_SUITE.erl

**New regression tests:**
- `user_with_sm_goes_offline_cleanly_sends_unavailable_presence` - Verifies immediate unavailable presence on clean disconnect
- `user_with_sm_killed_connection_sends_unavailable_presence_after_resume_timeout` - Verifies unavailable presence after resume timeout expires

**Updated existing tests:**
- Modified tests to handle additional presence stanzas from the fix
- Enhanced stanza counting and filtering to accommodate proper presence notifications
- Added presence stanza validation in resume scenarios

### Testing Strategy
- **Direct presence subscriptions**: Users establish presence relationships and verify unavailable notifications
- **Network failure simulation**: Connection killing with resume timeout validation  
- **Timing verification**: Ensures immediate notification on clean disconnect vs. delayed notification after resume timeout
- **Multi-resource scenarios**: Validates proper filtering when users have multiple active sessions

### Impact & Benefits
**XMPP Compliance**: Restores RFC 6121 compliance for presence subscriptions  
**Backward Compatibility**: No breaking changes to existing Stream Management functionality  
**Performance**: Minimal overhead with targeted presence filtering  
**Reliability**: Consistent presence state across clean and unclean disconnections  
**Multi-device Support**: Proper handling of users with multiple active resources  

### Verification
This fix ensures that:
1. Clean disconnections immediately send unavailable presence
2. Network failures send unavailable presence after resume timeout
3. Session resumption doesn't trigger unnecessary presence notifications
4. Multi-resource users receive proper presence filtering
5. All existing Stream Management features continue to work correctly

The changes restore the expected XMPP behavior where presence subscribers are always notified when users go offline, regardless of whether they have Stream Management enabled.

body:
## Purpose

The user requested to implement a preview page that admins are directed to after completing the biometric verification section in the template builder. This page should allow admins to preview how the verification form will appear to both administrators and end users (receivers) before finalizing the template.

## Code changes

- **Added new Preview component** (`client/pages/Preview.tsx`) with:
  - Admin and receiver view tabs in sidebar
  - Complete form preview showing personal information, document verification, and biometric verification sections
  - Header with save and send invite functionality
  - Step indicator showing current progress
  - Responsive design using modern CSS techniques

- **Updated routing** in `App.tsx`:
  - Added `/preview` and `/preview/:templateId` routes
  - Imported Preview component

- **Enhanced TemplateBuilder** navigation:
  - Added navigation to preview page when all sections are completed
  - Passes template data and configuration via route state

- **Updated Templates page**:
  - Added preview and edit actions for existing templates
  - Improved navigation handling for template actions
  - Code formatting improvements for better readability

author: rahim-kanji
body:
### Summary:
When executing the following **SET** command:

`SET datestyle='iso, mdy';`

the regex pattern used to parse the **SET** statement fails due to the space after the comma. As a result, the session gets **locked on the hostgroup**.

If the space is removed, i.e.:

`SET datestyle='iso,mdy';`

then the parsing works correctly and no lock occurs.

**Fix**
Update the regex pattern for **SET** parsing to allow optional spaces after commas in values.

Closes #[5101](https://github.com/sysown/proxysql/issues/5101)
